entries.title: Kindle+ is heavily discounted for Black Friday
entries.summary: Kindle+ offers 3 months for $0.99 for new members, running through November 30, 2026. The post Kindle+ is heavily discounted for Black Friday first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Kindle+, according to social media posts, is running a Black Friday/Cyber Monday promotion offering 3 months of Kindle+ for $0.99 to new members. Some users claim the promo code HPLUSMONTH also works for the discount. After the 3-month trial, it will cost $11.99/month recurring.

Kindle+ (rebranded from Kindle Unlimited in October 2026) is Amazon’s monthly digital subscription service that lets you read and listen to four million e-books, audiobooks, magazines, and comics. Borrow up to 20 titles simultaneously and keep them as long as your subscription is active. Magazines also count toward your 20-title limit. Read or listen on any Kindle e-reader, smartphone, tablet, or computer via the free Kindle app.

Michael Kozlowski is the editor-in-chief at Good e-Reader and has written about audiobooks and e-readers for the past fifteen years. Newspapers and websites such as the CBC, CNET, Engadget, Huffington Post and the New York Times have picked up his articles. He Lives in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

entries.title: Audible is giving a 3-month subscription for 0.99 per month
entries.summary: Audible Black Friday Deal: $0.99 Per Month + $20 in Audible Credit for Audible Standard. The post Audible is giving a 3-month subscription for 0.99 per month first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Audible is running a holiday promotion offering 3 months of Audible Standard for $0.99/month through December 28, 2026. You can claim this deal directly through Audible Canada or Amazon.ca, or through Audible US if you use a US account; it currently includes an extra $20 promotional credit.

This promotion is available to new members and eligible returning subscribers who are not currently enrolled in a membership or trial. US accounts are also restricted if you have redeemed more than two Audible promotional offers in the past 14 months. After the first 3 months, the plan automatically renews at the regular rate of $8.99/month (plus tax), though you can cancel anytime in your account settings before the fourth month bills.

Audible Standard lets you select 1 audiobook per month from the full catalog, plus unlimited access to select podcasts and Originals. Unlike Audible Premium Plus, audiobooks selected under the Standard plan are only playable while your membership remains active, and unused monthly selections do not roll over.

entries.title: Kindle Colorsoft 2024 Signature Edition vs Kindle Colorsoft 2026
entries.summary: The 2026 plastic Kindle Colorsoft improves on the original 2024 model with a thinner, lighter squared-off body, a user-replaceable battery, and an upgraded light guide that fixes early yellow-band screen issues, though it drops from 32GB to 16GB of storage and loses wireless charging and auto-brightness. The post Kindle Colorsoft 2024 Signature Edition vs Kindle Colorsoft 2026 first appeared on Go
entries.content:
The 2026 Kindle Colorsoft 16GB with a Plastic Body is thinner and lighter than the original 2024 Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition, which also has a plastic body. The 2026 model has a user-replaceable battery and a refined display stack—though it drops to 16GB of storage and removes wireless charging.

Built on the 2026 Paperwhite frame, the standard Colorsoft is a full millimeter thinner (6.8 mm) and 15 grams lighter than the 2024 release. According to Good e-Reader, the squared-off edges and relocated top-right power button prevent accidental presses while reading. It also swaps the 2024 rainbow-embossed rear logo for a standard embossed Kindle logo.

Both devices still rely on a 7-inch E Ink Kaleido 3 panel (300 ppi black-and-white, 150 ppi color) rather than moving to Kaleido 4. However, the 2026 model introduces a reworked reverse-stack construction with nitride LEDs, micro-deflectors, and an updated optical coating to improve light uniformity and address the yellow band discoloration seen on early 2024 units.

To comply with EU right-to-repair rules, the 2026 plastic back panel gently pries off from a corner, allowing you to unscrew and swap the battery yourself with a standard Phillips screwdriver.

Because Amazon split the 2026 lineup into a standard plastic tier and an aluminum Signature Edition, choosing the 2026 plastic model means giving up the 2024 model’s 32 GB storage, Qi wireless charging, and ambient auto-adjusting front light for a slimmer chassis and better repairability. (Note: The 2026 plastic model also lacks the magnetic pogo pins required for the new physical Page Turn Cover and charging dock, which are exclusive to the aluminum Signature Edition.)

Feature

2024 Kindle Colorsoft (Signature)

 2026 Kindle Colorsoft (Standard Plastic)
Body & Chassis Plastic with rounded edges Thinner, squared-off plastic
Thickness & Weight 7.8 mm / 219 g (7.7 oz) 6.8 mm / 204 g (7.2 oz)
Power Button Bottom edge Top-right side edge
Display Tech 7″ Kaleido 3 (300/150 ppi) 7″ Kaleido 3 + nitride LEDs & new optical coating
Storage 32 GB 16 GB
Battery Sealed (8 weeks) User-replaceable (8 weeks)
Extras Wireless charging & auto-brightness Manual warm light only (no wireless charging)

  • Read in color – The 7" Colorsoft display is high-contrast and easy on the eyes, with paper-like color that brings covers and content to life.
  • Color your pages – Highlight your favorite scenes in yellow, orange, blue, pink, and green
  • Marathon reading – A single charge via USB-C lasts up to 8 weeks, or power up with the wireless charging dock (sold separately).

Amazon Kindle Colorsoft 16GB (2026 model), Now thinner and lighter, 7" color display, Warm light...

  • The new Kindle Colorsoft — Thinner and lighter, with a 7" paper-like color display. New edge-to-edge color, waterproof design, no ads.

  • Up to 8 weeks on a single charge — The display only uses power when you turn the page or use the front light.

entries.title: Remarkable Tablets on Sale for Black Friday
entries.summary: For Black Friday 2026, reMarkable is offering $100 off standalone bundles and $300 off its Super Bundle, with deals running from November 19 through December 1, 2026 in North America. The post Remarkable Tablets on Sale for Black Friday first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
reMarkable is offering Black Friday bundle discounts of $100 off individual Paper Pro and Paper Pro Move bundles, or $300 off the two-tablet Super Bundle through December 1, 2026. The promotion launched in the US on November 19, 2026, through the reMarkable US Black Friday Store and major US retailers including Best Buy USA and Amazon.com. Standalone tablets without a folio and the monochrome reMarkable Paper Pure are excluded from the Black Friday markdowns.

Reviewers praise the reMarkable Paper Pro Move with Marker Plus and Basalt Book Folio for its pen-on-paper writing feel, crisp 264 PPI color display, and ultra-portable 230g frame, though many criticize its high price, narrow 16:9 aspect ratio, and reliance on a paid subscription for full search and cloud features. This bundle is widely viewed as a strong “sidekick” notebook for meetings, travel, and quick jotting, rather than a standalone replacement for a full-size document reader or multi-purpose tablet.

The reMarkable 2 with Marker Plus and Black Leather Book Folio is an older-generation monochrome paper tablet bundle that is excluded from the official Black Friday sale, though it remains available via third-party retailers and as a $399 USD refurbished bundle directly from reMarkable.

People like the reMarkable Paper Pro with Marker Plus and Black Leather Book Folio for its expansive 11.8-inch color canvas, snappy performance, and tactile pen-on-paper writing feel, though long-term users note trade-offs including muted screen contrast, added weight, edge wear on the leather folio, and a subscription requirement for full cloud features. This flagship bundle is widely regarded as an ideal desk-based digital notebook for annotating full-size PDFs, sketching, and distraction-free writing, rather than a lightweight e-reader or an all-in-one productivity tablet.

entries.title: Viwoods e-readers on sale for Black Friday
entries.summary: Viwoods is offering Black Friday discounts of up to 30% off across its e-reader and digital paper tablet lineup. The post Viwoods e-readers on sale for Black Friday first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Viwoods is offering Black Friday discounts of up to 30% off across its e-reader and digital paper tablet lineup, with sales running on the Viwoods Official Store and Amazon from November 19 to November 30, 2026.

Reviewers praise the VIWOODS AiPaper Reader for its remarkably slim 6.7 mm, 138-gram phone-style design, crisp 300 PPI Carta 1300 E Ink screen, full Google Play Store access via Android 16, and rare built-in 4G SIM support for reading on the go. Its dedicated physical AI button and Knowledge Base also earn solid marks for quickly summarizing passages or organizing research notes, though testers at Lifehacker and eWritable note meaningful compromises made to achieve that thin profile—most notably the lack of a warm front-light, built-in speakers, waterproofing, and microSD expansion. Overall, critics view it as a sleek, ultra-portable companion for distraction-free reading and mobile research, provided you don’t mind cool-toned night lighting and using Bluetooth headphones for audiobooks.

The 10.65-inch Viwoods AiPaper is praised for its remarkably thin 4.5 mm, 370-gram build, bright Carta 1300 Mobius display, and responsive, paper-like writing feel, paired with an included Wacom-compatible stylus. Critics at TechRadar and Lifehacker highlight its clean productivity layout—featuring dedicated Daily, Meeting, and Learning sections alongside Google Play Store support and quick AI tools for summarizing or converting handwriting—though they note drawbacks including the lack of a built-in front light, occasional ghosting or multitasking slowdowns, and a premium price tag. Ultimately, reviewers view it as one of the lightest and most capable large-screen E Ink notebooks for daytime note-taking and PDF annotation, as long as you don’t mind using an external lamp for night reading.

The VIWOODS AiPaper Mini is a compact, 8.2-inch Android E Ink tablet that bridges the gap between the pocket-sized AiPaper Reader and the 10.65-inch flagship AiPaper—adding a built-in front light while keeping full Wacom stylus support.

entries.summary: XTEINK is running its official Black Friday sale from November 19 to November 30, 2026, featuring discounts of up to 25% off on its official storefront alongside markdowns at retailers like Amazon. The post XTEINK E-readers on sale for Black Friday first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
XTEINK is running its official Black Friday sale from November 19 to November 30, 2026, featuring discounts of up to 25% off on its official storefront alongside markdowns at retailers like Amazon.

The XTEINK X4 Classic is an ultra-thin, distraction-free pocket e-reader built for extreme portability and pure daytime reading. Measuring just 4.9 mm thick and weighing 68 grams, it disappears easily into a pocket or attaches magnetically to the back of a smartphone via its built-in MagSafe-style ring. Because it omits both a touchscreen and a front-light layer over its 4.3-inch (219 PPI) E Ink display, reviewers note that text looks remarkably crisp and high-contrast in natural light. Upgraded internals—including a faster ESP32-S3 chip and a larger 920 mAh battery—deliver snappy page turns via tactile physical buttons or a built-in tilt-to-turn gyroscope, while stretching battery life to roughly two to three weeks per charge.

The XTEINK X3 is an ultra-compact, credit-card-sized pocket e-reader designed as an anti-doomscrolling companion that snaps magnetically onto the back of a smartphone without blocking camera bumps. Weighing just 58 grams and measuring 5.1 mm thick, it features a sharp 3.7-inch (259 PPI) E Ink display that delivers high-contrast, glare-free text without fading in direct sunlight, paired with tactile physical buttons, a tilt-to-turn gyroscope, and multi-week battery life from its 650 mAh cell. However, achieving this tiny footprint comes with clear compromises: it lacks a built-in front light for dark-room reading, swaps USB-C for a proprietary magnetic pogo-pin charger, and only supports DRM-free sideloaded files (such as EPUB and TXT) via microSD or companion transfer rather than locked Kindle or Libby books. While its stock interface is bare-bones and clunky, reviewers note that flashing open-source community firmware like CrossPoint transforms it into a snappy, highly customizable micro-reader ideal for daytime commutes and quick reading sessions.

entries.title: Kindle e-Readers have new Atkinson Hyperlegible font
entries.summary: The new Atkinson Hyperlegible font is available on all 2026 Kindle e-readers, Alexa Tablets, and the Kindle app for Android and iOS starting today. The post Kindle e-Readers have new Atkinson Hyperlegible font first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon Kindle e-readers now have a new font called Atkinson Hyperlegible. Developed by the Braille Institute, it makes letters and numbers clearly distinct, making words more legible and every page more comfortable to read for individuals with low vision.

Atkinson Hyperlegible works great for body text, UI elements, and captions, but can look a bit plain, utilitarian, or spacious when scaled up too large for a main display header. It clearly differentiates commonly confused shapes, such as lowercase l, uppercase I, and 1, as well as 0 and O, or B and 8, by adding distinct tails, serifs, and open counters. While many readers with dyslexia find it easier to read because of the sharp character distinction, it wasn’t built strictly for dyslexia, and some readers still mix up similar letters like p, q, and b.

The award-winning font has made reading easier for millions upon millions of people and continues to change lives daily. The Kindle e-readers released in 2026, Alexa Tablets, and the Kindle app for Android and iOS all include it.

Kindle users can also modify the margins, spacing (including between lines, paragraphs, words, and characters), alignment, and page color (including “dark mode”). For some readers, choosing left-aligned text (vs. fully justified), plus wider spacing and margins, can reduce eye strain and improve focus. The option to create custom themes makes it easy to save and reuse your preferred settings. Current-generation Kindle devices also allow users to adjust the text size in the user interface to make it easier to read.

entries.title: When will we see E INK Kaleido 4 e-readers?
entries.summary: Industry reports from Good e-Reader indicate these manufacturers will roll out the first wave of international Kaleido 4 e-readers and e-notes in 2027, with a new Kindle Scribe in 2028. The post When will we see E INK Kaleido 4 e-readers? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Announced in October 2026, E Ink Kaleido 4 is the fourth-generation color e-paper display technology designed for e-readers and digital notebooks. It builds on the E Ink Kaleido color filter array architecture with faster refresh performance, stronger contrast, and a wider color range than Kaleido 3. When will we start to see e-readers using this technology?

Compared to the previous generation, E Ink Kaleido 4 doubles its color gamut volume to more than 40K, increases white reflectance by 15%, and improves contrast by 50%. Additionally, with the introduction of new algorithms, E Ink Kaleido 4 is capable of video playback at up to 18 frames per second. These enhancements let color e-paper display text, images, charts, presentations, and video more clearly while reducing the perception of screen graininess.

E Ink Kaleido 4 incorporates a new oxide TFT backplane that supports higher driving voltages and faster screen refresh. Combined with Hanvon Technology’s proprietary “Enhanced Pressure Floating” technology and T2000 timing controller, it enables 27% faster page turning and scrolling on the M10C II. A redesigned front-light system also delivers clearer, more natural color reproduction.

E. INK has confirmed with Good e-Reader that the color resolution has been increased to 300 PPI, whereas Kaleido 3 could only do 150 PPI. This will dramatically increase the number of colors, giving cover art, images, e-textbooks, and PDF files more contrast and a less grainy look.

The first product to use Kaleido 4 is the Hanvon M10C III, but the prices and release date are unknown. The device will only be available in China. The M10C II pairs E Ink Kaleido 4 with Hanvon Technology’s OCR, voice, and AI-powered office applications, along with features such as cloud library synchronization, ripple-reduction technology, responsive third-party app scaling, and optimized font rendering. For handwriting, its wireless, battery-free digital pen offers 8,192 levels of pressure sensitivity, while a micro-etched tempered-glass surface reduces glare and parallax and further provides a paper-like writing resistance. Together, these capabilities create a smoother experience for reading, writing, note-taking, and on-the-go productivity.

“The global debut of the M10C II featuring E Ink Kaleido 4 is not simply a screen upgrade,” said Wang Jie, Vice President of Hanvon Technology. “Built around next-generation color ePaper, we have systematically optimized the display, fast refresh, handwriting, recording and AI capabilities. With the M10C II, we hope to take color ePaper beyond reading devices and into productivity scenarios such as R&D tools, professional document review, meeting records and mobile office applications.”

When will we see Kaleido 4 in e-readers?

E-Ink has to undergo mass manufacturing for the new Kaleido 4 e-paper panels, and everyone is going to be jumping over it. The main selling point is 300 PPI for color, up from 150 PPI on Kaleido 3. It can also display 40,000 colors, instead of 4096 found on Kaleido 3. The revised front-lit display and the ability to display YouTube videos or full motion video will ensure that Android e-readers from Onyx Boox, Bigme, and monitors will really take advantage of this tech.

Amazon just refreshed their entire Kindle product line for consumer-grade e-readers, so it will be late 2027 or 2028 before they update the Kindle Scribe with the new color e-paper panels. Likely, Rakuten Kobo will be the first ones in North America to release a Kaleido 4 e-reader, since their older devices were released in 2024. PocketBook will also be among the first to release a new model.

entries.title: Manga Million launches worldwide with 100 Digital Manga
entries.summary: Manga Million has launched with 1,000 pages of translated manga avaialble for free, with no accounts or registration required. The post Manga Million launches worldwide with 100 Digital Manga first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Shueisha announced the launch of its global digital manga platform, MANGA MILLION, which will be available in more than 100 languages, including English, Chinese, Hindi, Arabic, Spanish, French, Turkish, Tagalog, Korean, and Polish. At launch, the platform features over one million pages of translated manga from 400 titles.

The company stated that over 150 of those titles are shojo manga. The titles include ONE PIECE, Naruto, Bleach, Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba, Jujutsu Kaisen, Kingdom, Oshi no Ko, SPY×FAMILY, Chainsaw Man, NANA, Kimi ni Todoke – From Me to You, and more.

Editor-in-Chief of MANGA Plus at Shueisha, Shuhei Hosono, initiated the MANGA MILLION project and said of the launch: The project began with a simple question: what if we marked Shueisha’s 100th anniversary by translating one million pages of manga into 100 languages? As we developed the concept, we also saw it as a way to address the language barriers that still prevent many readers around the world from accessing manga. We hope that MANGA MILLION, an unprecedented translation initiative spanning 100 languages and one million pages, will spark new discoveries and connections between readers and Japanese manga.

Users can access everything for free, with no registration required. In keeping with the theme of its 100th anniversary, MANGA MILLION offers a collection of one million pages of Shueisha manga in over 100 languages. The people who run this also run Manga Plus, which has been very successful.
